source.title: Compressible Dynamics in Deep Overparameterized Low-Rank Learning & Adaptation
source.authors: Can Yaras; Peng Wang; Laura Balzano; Qing Qu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different low-rank fine-tuning method changes held-out validation performance and overfitting, but does not test the listed claim versions' specified settings or measures.
record.gate_note: Deep LoRA versus vanilla LoRA validation results and reported overfitting behavior bear on generalization, but not on any version's specified models, interventions, or measures. Figure 2 concerns matrix completion and is not a result on natural-label generalization.
record.test_reason: The study tests compression and deep low-rank adaptation, not any of V1–V8. Its validation comparisons concern adaptation depth, and its matrix-completion width experiments concern recovery and convergence. Neither establishes decreasing classification test error beyond the width needed for interpolation in V2. Adam is used for both adaptation methods; optimizer, batch-size and dropout effects are not compared.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors report better limited-data language-task validation performance, lower-rank updates and greater rank robustness with Deep LoRA, and interpret these as reduced overfitting from depth. Generation gains exclude METEOR. Their central contribution also includes theoretical invariant subspaces and compression that preserves useful learning dynamics with improved efficiency.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares compressed three-layer Deep LoRA updates with vanilla two-layer LoRA for pretrained-model fine-tuning; this differs from the claim versions' interventions and settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The validation performance comparison varies by GLUE task and NLG metric; METEOR is slightly worse for Deep LoRA. STS-B few-shot comparisons vary training sample size.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep LoRA improves validation performance over vanilla LoRA on all eight reported GLUE tasks with 1024 training examples; the overall reported difference is +0.028.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep LoRA improves limited-data BERT adaptation performance over vanilla LoRA under the tested training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.2 reports higher Deep LoRA validation performance at all three STS-B sample sizes, with the largest difference at 16 examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep LoRA improves few-shot STS-B validation performance over vanilla LoRA at the tested sample sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep LoRA improves BLEU and four ROUGE metrics on 16-example E2E adaptation, while METEOR decreases by 0.00036.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep LoRA's few-shot T5 generation gains depend on the evaluation metric.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 and Section 3 report that deeper matrix factorizations resist overfitting when rank is overestimated, while additional width accelerates convergence. Figure 8 reports greater adaptation-rank robustness for Deep LoRA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth can improve robustness to overestimated factorization rank in matrix completion and limited-data language-model adaptation.

record.problems: The reported language-model evidence compares validation performance between methods and does not report the train-test error gap or random-label memorization. Several figure results provide no numeric values in the text. Table 1 does not name the performance metric in the table.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 8 rank-robustness results and Figures 2, 5, 7, 10, and 11 were left out because they concern rank, matrix recovery, efficiency, or convergence rather than the claim's listed measures of natural-label generalization gap. Figure 6 is included as figure-only rows for its stated validation-performance comparison.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting capacity together with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Whether widening ReLU classifiers beyond the width needed for zero training error continues lowering test error. Rank robustness and matrix-completion convergence do not establish this.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier performance and the contribution of local connectivity or convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, and recovery through weight decay or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their performance difference.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including small-data, excessive-dropout and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and its ranking relative to norm- or margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain outside V1–V8; cannot_determine denotes their inability to establish a listed version, not uncertainty about the reported table differences. The absence of a train–test gap alone would not exclude a study: these versions also include direct held-out-performance comparisons, but the required interventions are absent here.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label accuracy for the specified architectures and datasets.
One-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the specified local-connectivity comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the stated benchmark and tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects in the specified classifier regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
